patches.replacement: The finite calculations below use exact integer algorithms, finite search domains and complete tables. For exactly two small entries whose product is not $-1$, we bound the third large entry and construct the graph on all common extensions inside that disk. Reversible descent proves completeness, and the absence of triangles excludes a sextuple. The pairs with product $-1$ are treated separately. For three small entries, a finite classification leaves at most one further entry below a fixed radius, and approximation estimates exclude three further entries.
patches.why: The current opening promises finite calculations but leaves their link to the six-entry obstruction implicit. This names the third-large-entry cutoff, explains why triangle-freeness suffices, and distinguishes the three-small route before the two long auxiliary proofs.
patches.contract: Orientation only. No theorem, proof, bound, algorithm, table, exception or label is changed. The graph claim is explicitly restricted to pairs with ab+1 nonzero. Small means modulus below 3 as already defined.
patches.check: Sentence by sentence against Section 7. A two-small sextuple has S,T,C below the cutoff, so they would give a triangle. Nondegenerate pairs have complete descent graphs. The two product-minus-one classes are treated separately. The triple table has at most one further entry within 10^40, and the final proposition rules out three further entries.

patches.replacement: If $x=\log_{10}S\ge49$, then $400<10^3$ gives $\log_{10}D>8x-3$. This contradicts~\eqref{sm:five-uniform-continuous}, since $(8x-3)-g(x)=x-227/5-(4047/25)/(x-4)$ is increasing and equals $1/375$ at $49$.
patches.why: The letter s already denotes the third tuple entry, and that meaning is needed again for the anchors (a,b,s) in the next case. Giving s the value log10(S) creates a genuine local notation collision. Use the dummy real variable x already used in the definition of g.
patches.contract: Only the dummy logarithmic variable changes. The same condition, lower bound, increasing difference and exact endpoint value remain. Tuple entry s retains its original meaning.
